text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian newspapers this morning.

- The Norwegian Banking, Insurance and Securities Commission wants banks to fix new guidelines for granting mortgage loans. Recent surveys have revealed that 10 percent of house buyers borrow more than the properties are worth.
- Norway lacks a competent workforce. Recruitment consultants have plenty of work, but find it difficult to fill management jobs.

- Authorities are concerned about the number of diving accidents in Norway. Safety rules were introduced in 1995, however the number of accidents is at a standstill. Six people died while diving in both 1995 and 1996, while five divers have died so far this year.

- Per Olaf Lundteigen, member of parliament for the Centre Party, has suggested implementing the taxation model used in Norway's shipping industry in industry in general. Lundteigen sees favourable tax rules as a way of preventing companies such as drugs group Nycomed ASA from moving abroad.
- Regional hospitals buy equipment and services for 14 billion crowns per year, but only 26 percent comes from Norwegian suppliers.
- A new mesurement system commissioned by Fred Olsen & Co could reduce the danger of oil spills and provide valuable information on the condition of hulls of ageing tankers.
